Thoracic surgery treats diseases of the organs and tissues within the chest, excluding the heart, including the lungs, airways, chest wall, pleura, diaphragm, mediastinum and oesophagus. The department uses fibreoptic and endoscopic equipment, minimally invasive surgical tools and imaging from virtual bronchoscopy to PET-CT, supported by pathology and laboratory services. MedLuxLife coordinates evaluation and surgery at our partner hospital, from your first consultation with the specialist to planning your recovery stay.

Urology covers the diagnosis and treatment of conditions of the urinary tract in women and men and of the male reproductive organs, from urological cancers and prostate disease to kidney stones, infertility and incontinence. Care is personalised and coordinated with internal medicine, oncology, gynaecology and psychiatry when needed. MedLuxLife arranges consultations and treatment at our partner hospital and supports you before, during and after your stay.
Diagnosis and treatment of prostate, bladder, kidney and testicular cancer.
Treatment options for an enlarged prostate, including laser prostate surgery (GreenLight).
HIFU focal therapy may be an option for suitable patients with prostate cancer.
Treatment of kidney stones with flexible endoscopic methods and treatment of urinary tract stones.
Assessment and treatment of male infertility and erectile problems.
Diagnosis and treatment of urinary incontinence, female sexual dysfunction and conditions of the urinary tract and pelvic organs.
Collaboration with internal medicine, oncology, obstetrics and gynaecology, and psychiatry where appropriate.
Conditions of the female urinary tract and pelvic organs
Plan your Urology consultation with confidence

Internal medicine is often the first point of contact for adult health problems and covers a very wide range of conditions, from high blood pressure to diseases of the kidneys, liver and blood. At our partner hospital it brings together several subspecialties under one roof. MedLuxLife helps you find the right specialist, arranges appointments and tests, and coordinates follow-up with your doctor at home.
Care for hormone and metabolic disorders such as diabetes and thyroid disease.
Assessment and treatment of digestive system and liver conditions.
Comprehensive evaluation of adult health problems and coordination with other specialists.
Diagnosis and treatment of blood disorders.
Care for kidney diseases and related conditions such as hypertension.
Diagnosis and management of rheumatic and inflammatory joint diseases.
Upper and lower respiratory tract diseases
Plan your Internal Medicine consultation with confidence

Endocrinology deals with the hormone-producing glands and the metabolic conditions they influence, such as diabetes, thyroid disorders and diseases of the pituitary and adrenal glands. Most of these conditions are diagnosed with blood tests and imaging and treated with medication and lifestyle measures, with long-term follow-up. MedLuxLife arranges a consultation with an endocrinologist at our partner hospital and coordinates any further tests or treatment.
For surgical treatment of the thyroid, parathyroid and adrenal glands, see
Diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of type 1 and type 2 diabetes, including insulin therapy, modern oral and injectable medicines and screening for complications.
Treatment of an underactive or overactive thyroid (hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism), Hashimoto’s and Graves’ disease, and assessment of thyroid nodules.
Diagnosis and treatment of pituitary tumours and hormone imbalances, in cooperation with the pituitary clinic and neurosurgery.
Assessment of adrenal gland disorders such as Cushing’s syndrome, Addison’s disease, hyperaldosteronism and adrenal masses.
Diagnosis and treatment of osteoporosis, vitamin D deficiency and parathyroid hormone disorders.
Medical assessment of weight-related metabolic problems, insulin resistance and metabolic syndrome, with referral to nutrition or obesity surgery where suitable.
Diagnosis and treatment of high cholesterol and triglyceride levels to reduce cardiovascular risk.
Hormonal causes of irregular periods, hirsutism, PCOS, low testosterone and menopause-related complaints.
Dynamic hormone stimulation and suppression tests
Oral glucose tolerance test and HbA1c
Fine-needle aspiration biopsy of thyroid nodules
Imaging of the pituitary and adrenal glands in cooperation with radiology
Recent hormone test results (for example thyroid tests, HbA1c)
Your current insulin or hormone doses

This multidisciplinary clinic is dedicated exclusively to diseases of the thyroid and parathyroid glands, offering early diagnosis together with medical and surgical treatment. Specialists from seven fields evaluate each case jointly, following current scientific evidence. MedLuxLife coordinates your assessment, tests and any surgery at our partner hospital, with clear communication at every stage.

original: Pituitary disorders can be difficult to recognise because their symptoms often resemble other illnesses, so early and accurate diagnosis matters. This dedicated clinic brings several specialties together to evaluate pituitary diseases and tumours and to plan diagnosis and treatment using modern imaging, laboratory and treatment methods. MedLuxLife coordinates your referral, records and appointments at our partner hospital.
Focused assessment of symptoms, hormone levels and imaging to identify pituitary conditions as early as possible.
Evaluation and treatment planning for pituitary tumours and other diseases of the gland.

Care involves endocrinologists specialised in pituitary disease, neurosurgeons, neuroradiologists, neuropathologists, neuro-ophthalmologists, radiation oncologists, anaesthesiologists and supporting health staff.
Pituitary cases are discussed at regular multidisciplinary meetings, which external physicians can also attend with their own cases.
The clinic runs educational programmes on pituitary disease for patients and physicians.
The clinic works together with international organisations in the field of pituitary disease.

Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, colonoscopy and double-balloon endoscopy (enteroscopy), which can examine parts of the small intestine beyond the reach of standard scopes, for example in unexplained bleeding, iron-deficiency anaemia or suspected Crohn’s disease.
Band ligation, sclerotherapy, haemoclips and argon laser treatment for bleeding from the stomach or intestines.
Balloon dilatation and stent placement for strictures of the stomach or intestines.
Intragastric balloon placement during upper endoscopy, which may support weight loss alongside lifestyle changes; the balloon is removed after a set period.

Upper endoscopy, 24-hour pH monitoring and motility studies, followed by medication, endoscopic options such as the Stretta procedure and endoscopic fundoplication (for example Plicator or Gastrofix), or surgery.
Urea breath test and stool antigen testing to diagnose H. pylori infection and guide treatment.
Screening colonoscopy with polypectomy, as polyps can be found and removed during the procedure; people at higher risk receive an individual screening plan.
Endoscopic imaging of the bile and pancreatic ducts, which also allows stone removal, stent placement to relieve blockages and biopsy.
Medication for early stages and band ligation, sclerotherapy, laser or infrared treatment during sedated colonoscopy for intermediate stages, with referral for surgery in advanced cases.

Diagnosis and long-term follow-up of chronic hepatitis B and C using liver function tests, HBV and HCV PCR, abdominal ultrasound and liver biopsy, with antiviral treatment options including interferon.
Diagnosis of ulcerative colitis and Crohn’s disease by colonoscopy and/or double-balloon enteroscopy, and ongoing medical treatment.
Previous endoscopy or colonoscopy reports with pathology results
Recent liver function and hepatitis test results, if relevant
Plan your Gastroenterology consultation with confidence

Gastroenterology covers the evaluation, diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the stomach, intestines, liver, bile ducts and pancreas. The department at our partner hospital offers a wide range of diagnostic and therapeutic endoscopy, alongside dedicated care for reflux, liver disease, inflammatory bowel disease and colorectal cancer screening. MedLuxLife helps you arrange procedures and understand preparation instructions; the hospital gives you your reports for your doctor at home.

Nephrology is the branch of internal medicine concerned with kidney health and disease, including blood pressure, fluid and electrolyte balance, and the effects of other illnesses and medicines on the kidneys. At our partner hospital, nephrologists provide outpatient, inpatient and intensive care services, all forms of dialysis and assessment for kidney transplantation with lifelong follow-up. MedLuxLife coordinates your appointments and treatment schedule and organises the practical details of your stay.
Diagnosis and treatment of kidney diseases, preventive care for people at higher risk such as those with diabetes or hypertension, and supportive care for advanced kidney disease.
Ward-based care and follow-up, plus nephrology consultations for other departments.
Kidney effects of other conditions and medicines
Evaluation of how diabetes, hypertension, rheumatological disease, acute illness or long-term medicines such as chemotherapy, anti-rheumatic drugs and cortisone may affect the kidneys.
Haemodialysis, haemofiltration, haemodiafiltration and continuous venovenous haemofiltration for patients with acute kidney failure.
Blood purification treatments that may be used when clinically indicated.
Acute or chronic haemodialysis, with session frequency and length adjusted to remaining kidney function and diet.
Peritoneal dialysis including continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis (CAPD), which patients perform themselves at home.
Assessment for transplantation in end-stage kidney disease, with transplantation through the organ transplant unit and lifelong post-transplant follow-up.
Structural and functional disorders of the urinary system
Kidney problems related to fluid loss, heart failure or sepsis
Recent kidney function and urine test results
Dialysis prescription and session records, if on dialysis
Plan your Nephrology consultation with confidence
Assessment, diagnosis and individual treatment planning for adults with respiratory symptoms or known lung disease.
Examination of the airways with a flexible camera to support diagnosis and, where needed, treatment.
Breathing tests that measure how well the lungs are working.
Skin tests that can help identify allergic triggers for respiratory symptoms.
Counselling and follow-up for people who want to stop smoking.
Ongoing physician follow-up and adjustment of treatment for chronic lung conditions.
Lung disease caused by occupational exposure
Chest X-ray or CT images with reports
Plan your Chest Diseases (Pulmonology) consultation with confidence

Chest diseases, or pulmonology, covers the diagnosis, treatment and long-term follow-up of conditions affecting the lungs and airways. The department at our partner hospital serves adult patients through its outpatient clinic, bronchoscopy unit, pulmonary function laboratory and allergy skin testing. MedLuxLife coordinates your appointments; previous scans and lung function results go directly to the specialist, for example in your online consultation.

This department diagnoses, treats and follows up infections caused by bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites, using up-to-date laboratory and, where needed, molecular methods. It also advises on vaccination, prevention and travel medicine. MedLuxLife arranges outpatient or inpatient care at our partner hospital and handles the practical details so you can focus on recovery.
Diagnosis and treatment of infectious diseases in the outpatient clinic or on the ward, depending on the patient’s condition.
Advanced laboratory techniques and molecular methods are used when needed to plan the diagnostic process.
Guidance on vaccines that can help protect against infectious diseases.
Advice on practical methods to reduce the risk of infection.
Consultation before or after travel on infections, vaccines and precautions relevant to your destination.
A hospital infection control committee oversees hygiene, with up-to-date air and surface disinfection and dedicated bed-cleaning systems to help reduce hospital-acquired infections.
Jaundice (hepatitis A, hepatitis B, hepatitis C and others)
Recent microbiology, culture or serology results
Vaccination record and recent travel history
Plan your Infectious Diseases and Clinical Microbiology consultation with confidence

Immunology deals with diseases of the immune system, which can be difficult to recognise because symptoms are not always obvious. Specialists at our partner hospital combine careful clinical evaluation with an advanced laboratory to reach a diagnosis and design a personal treatment plan. MedLuxLife coordinates your tests and consultations and helps you take the results and recommendations home with you.
A thorough evaluation supported by blood tests, immunophenotyping, tissue typing, antibody profiles, allergy tests and other laboratory methods.
Treatment is tailored to each patient and may include medication and immunoglobulin therapy, aiming to ease symptoms and slow disease progression.
Advice on nutrition, exercise and sleep for patients with weakened immunity, provided together with other units of the hospital.
Vaccines and preventive measures recommended for people who are prone to immune system disorders, to help lower the risk of infection.
Previous immunology and allergy test results
A list of past infections and vaccinations
Plan your Immunology consultation with confidence

Dermatology covers the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of conditions affecting the skin, hair and nails. Alongside medical dermatology, the department at our partner hospital offers dermatosurgery, cosmetic dermatology and care for certain genital skin conditions. MedLuxLife arranges consultations and helps combine dermatology appointments with any other treatment you are planning during your stay.
Diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of a wide range of skin, hair and nail diseases.
Surgical procedures on the skin, for example for moles or skin lesions that need removal or examination.
Dermatocosmetic procedures including laser applications, botulinum toxin (Botox) and chemical peels.
Diagnosis and treatment of genital warts, molluscum, genital herpes, external genital fungal infections and syphilis.
Examination of moles and suspicious lesions, and treatment planning for skin cancers.
Photographs showing how the skin condition has changed over time
Previous skin biopsy or pathology reports
Plan your Dermatology consultation with confidence

Balanced nutrition plays an important part in both preventing illness and supporting medical treatment. The nutrition and dietetics team at our partner hospital assesses your eating habits and body composition and develops a personalised nutrition plan with regular follow-up. MedLuxLife coordinates your consultations and can combine them with other treatments during your stay.
Review of eating habits plus body analysis to measure fat, muscle and water percentages and regional fat distribution.
A plan based on age, height, sex, physical activity and blood test results, with regular follow-up appointments.
Menus for hospitalised patients are planned together with doctors, the patient and relatives, and monitored from preparation to delivery.
Guidance during the hospital stay on how to continue the nutrition plan at home.
Nutritional preparation before bariatric surgery to help reduce surgical risk, and guidance on sustainable lifestyle changes afterwards.
On request, follow-up at home for elderly or bedridden patients.
Nutrition and diet counselling and customised menu planning for private organisations.
Seminars, training sessions and media work to raise awareness of healthy eating.
Medical nutrition in high blood pressure and cardiovascular diseases
Medical nutrition for rheumatism and gout
Nutrition with food allergies and food intolerances
Healthy nutrition in infancy, childhood and adolescence
Healthy nutrition during pregnancy and breastfeeding
A short food diary of a typical week

The paediatrics department provides diagnosis and treatment for children from birth to 18 years of age, with outpatient clinics, an inpatient ward and intensive care areas designed for children. It is organised into a newborn section (0-28 days) and a child section (0-18 years), with subspecialties working together as a multidisciplinary team. MedLuxLife helps families access the right paediatric specialist at our partner hospital and coordinates appointments, travel and communication.
Outpatient, inpatient and intensive care services for children aged 0-18 in child-friendly settings.
The neonatal section serves babies up to 28 days old through a neonatal unit, a neonatal observation unit and a neonatal intensive care unit.
The hospital follows the UNICEF and WHO Baby-Friendly approach, with specially trained staff helping mothers establish and maintain breastfeeding.

Testing and treatment for allergic diseases, including skin tests, blood allergy tests, lung function tests, allergen provocation tests, food tests, anaesthetic drug tests and allergy vaccination (immunotherapy).
Assessment of hormonal and metabolic problems such as growth disorders, diabetes, thyroid and puberty-related conditions.
Diagnosis and treatment of blood diseases and childhood cancers, with outpatient and inpatient care in a paediatric bone marrow transplantation clinic.
Care for diseases of the oesophagus, stomach, duodenum, small and large intestine, liver and gallbladder, as well as nutritional disorders.

Treatment of urological, genital, digestive and respiratory conditions and newborn anomalies, including non-cardiac thoracic, oncological, digestive and endocrine surgery, paediatric gynaecology, trauma surgery, diagnostic and interventional endoscopy, and laparoscopic and thoracoscopic procedures.
Diagnosis and treatment of congenital and acquired problems of the kidneys, urinary tract, bladder and urethra.
Outpatient care for childhood rheumatic diseases affecting joints, muscles, blood vessels and skin.
Diseases of the oesophagus, stomach and intestines
Growth charts or previous paediatric reports
Plan your Paediatrics consultation with confidence

Paediatric surgery deals with conditions requiring surgical care in infants, children and adolescents, from the prenatal period up to the age of 18. Treatment is tailored to the child’s age and development, with open, endoscopic and laparoscopic techniques available. MedLuxLife coordinates consultations, surgery dates and aftercare at our partner hospital, so that families can focus on their child.
Surgical evaluation can begin before birth when a condition requiring surgery is identified during pregnancy.
Diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of surgical conditions affecting the digestive tract in children.
Surgical care for conditions of the kidneys, bladder and urinary tract in childhood.
Treatment of surgical conditions within the chest cavity, excluding the heart.
Alongside conventional surgery, endoscopic and laparoscopic methods are used where suitable.
Many procedures allow same-day discharge, including inguinal hernia repair, hydrocele repair, treatment of undescended testicles, circumcision, catheter placement and endoscopic procedures.
Specific pain-relief measures aim to keep children comfortable in hospital and after returning home.
In collaboration with the Urology department, surgical and endoscopic treatment of congenital anomalies and acquired problems such as stones and trauma.
Work with other specialties for conditions such as congenital spinal cord defects and nocturnal enuresis (bedwetting).
Vesicoureteral reflux (urine flowing back from the bladder to the kidneys)
Prenatal scan reports, if the condition was identified before birth

Paediatric cardiology looks after the heart and circulation of children from birth through adolescence. Specialists assess congenital and acquired heart conditions and plan treatment together with paediatric heart surgeons and other specialties. MedLuxLife arranges examinations and follow-up at our partner hospital and supports families during every visit.
Every assessment starts with a thorough examination by a paediatric cardiologist.
Heart ultrasound, electrocardiogram and other tests help establish the diagnosis.
Heart findings detected before birth by obstetricians are evaluated by paediatric cardiologists after delivery.
A treatment plan is prepared for each child, with regular monitoring of how treatment is progressing.
Some children need regular cardiac check-ups over many years, so close contact with the care team is maintained.
Collaboration with paediatric cardiac surgery, paediatric haematology and oncology, genetics and other paediatric specialties.
Prenatal heart scan findings, if any
Plan your Paediatric Cardiology consultation with confidence

Paediatric oncology focuses on the diagnosis, treatment and long-term follow-up of cancers in children and adolescents up to the age of 18, including solid tumours, lymphomas and leukaemias. Childhood cancers behave differently from adult cancers and call for care designed around young patients and their families. MedLuxLife coordinates assessments and treatment at our partner hospital, helping families with records, appointments, travel and communication throughout the course of care.
Thorough evaluation of suspected childhood tumours, lymphomas and leukaemias to establish the diagnosis and the extent of the disease.
Surgical removal of tumours may form part of the treatment plan, depending on tumour type and spread.
Drug-based cancer treatment planned individually for each child, delivered on an inpatient or outpatient basis.
Radiation treatment may be recommended for certain tumour types as part of a combined plan.
Treatments that engage the immune system can be considered for selected childhood cancers.
Stem cell transplantation is among the treatment options for some childhood cancers and blood diseases.
Outpatient and inpatient care in a dedicated paediatric haematology-oncology clinic, with single rooms that allow a parent to stay with the child during monitoring and treatment.
A day unit for short treatments and blood transfusions, so that many children can return home the same day.
Outpatient consultations take place on a separate floor reserved for children with cancer, leukaemia and blood diseases.
Structured follow-up after treatment to monitor recovery and the child’s ongoing health.
Wilms’ tumour and other kidney tumours
Soft tissue sarcomas (muscle and connective tissue tumours)
Previous imaging (MRI, CT or PET-CT) on CD/DVD with reports

Paediatric haematology covers blood disorders and childhood cancers from the newborn period to 18 years, with diagnosis and treatment adapted to children. The department works closely with the paediatric bone marrow transplantation clinic for both outpatient and inpatient care. MedLuxLife coordinates assessments, treatment schedules and family logistics at our partner hospital.
Diagnosis and treatment of anaemias, blood production disorders and bone marrow failure.
Care for leukaemia and other tumours in children, planned with child-specific approaches.
Follow-up of inherited blood and immune system disorders such as thalassaemia and sickle cell disease.
Outpatient and inpatient treatment in cooperation with the paediatric bone marrow transplantation clinic when needed.
Complete blood count history and haematology reports
Bone marrow or pathology reports, if available

Stem cell (bone marrow) transplantation is a treatment option for a range of hereditary and acquired diseases in children when other treatments are not sufficient. It is carried out by a specialised team in dedicated transplant units with strict infection control. MedLuxLife helps families with the assessment, planning and long stay that transplantation involves at our partner hospital.
A specialised treatment for selected children whose condition has not responded adequately to medical therapy.
Intensive therapy before and after the transplant, with close monitoring of the weakened immune system.
Single isolation rooms, filtered air, controlled access and strict hygiene rules help protect children from infection.
The transplant unit operates with intensive care standards throughout the treatment period.
Conditions that may be treated with transplantation
Complete haematology reports and bone marrow biopsy results

Paediatric neurology diagnoses and treats disorders of the brain, spinal cord, nerves and muscles in children from birth to 18 years. MedLuxLife coordinates consultations, investigations and follow-up at our partner hospital.
A detailed neurological examination by a paediatric neurologist, with MRI and EEG when considered necessary.
Monitoring and treatment of different seizure types and epilepsy in children.
Assessment of delays in motor skills such as walking, in speech and in cognitive development.
Care for muscle weakness, movement disorders and spinal muscular atrophy (SMA).
Management of inherited and congenital conditions affecting the nervous system.
Evaluation of headaches and fainting episodes in children.
Congenital diseases of the nervous system

Paediatric nephrology deals with diseases of the kidneys, urinary tract, bladder and urethra in children from birth to 18 years. Signs such as swelling of the hands, feet or eyes, blood in the urine or pain when passing urine should be assessed without delay. MedLuxLife arranges specialist consultations at our partner hospital, where care is multidisciplinary and families are supported at every stage.
Diagnosis and management of acute and chronic kidney failure in children.
Dialysis care for children who need kidney replacement therapy.
Care for children before and after kidney transplantation.
Evaluation and treatment of urinary tract infections and vesicoureteral reflux.
Follow-up of antenatal hydronephrosis and abnormalities of the urinary system.
Assessment and treatment of enuresis and kidney stone disease in children.
Recent urine and kidney function test results

Paediatric endocrinology covers hormonal, growth and metabolic disorders in children from the newborn period to 18 years. Treatment is planned with each child’s growth and stage of development in mind. MedLuxLife coordinates consultations, tests and follow-up appointments with specialists at our partner hospital.
Assessment of growth delay, short stature and developmental concerns.
Evaluation of early or delayed puberty and menstrual irregularities.
Diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of childhood diabetes, obesity and low blood sugar.
Care for disorders of the thyroid, adrenal and pituitary glands.
Investigation of calcium and bone metabolism disorders.
Evaluation of differences of sex development, including undescended testis and micropenis.

This department diagnoses and treats diseases of the digestive tract, liver and pancreas, as well as nutrition-related conditions, in children from infancy to 18 years. Assessment of disorders of the oesophagus, stomach and duodenum.
Diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the small and large intestine.
Paediatric hepatology care for liver and gallbladder conditions, and evaluation of pancreatic disorders.
Assessment and management of nutritional problems and nutrition-related diseases in children.
Diseases of the small and large intestine
Recent blood and stool test results

This department diagnoses and treats allergic conditions in children and adolescents from birth to 18 years. A range of skin, blood, breathing and provocation tests helps identify triggers so a suitable treatment plan can be made. Skin testing to identify substances that may trigger allergic reactions.
Laboratory tests to measure allergic sensitisation.
Respiratory function testing for children with asthma, wheezing or chronic cough.
Allergen provocation, food tests and anaesthetic drug tests carried out under medical supervision.

Children are more vulnerable to infections than other age groups, and some infections need specialist assessment and follow-up. Investigation of frequently recurring respiratory, gastrointestinal and urinary tract infections.
Diagnosis and care for illnesses such as measles, rubella, fifth disease and sixth disease.

Careful evaluation of joint, muscle, skin and systemic symptoms in children to reach a clear diagnosis.
Investigation of unexplained or recurring fevers, including possible autoinflammatory causes.
Diagnosis and treatment planning for juvenile arthritis and related joint conditions.
Care for conditions that inflame blood vessels or affect several organs at once.
Collaboration with other paediatric specialties when a condition involves more than the musculoskeletal system.
Ongoing monitoring to help control disease activity and support the child’s quality of life.

MedLuxLife helps families coordinate admission to the NICU at our partner hospital, arrange transfers and keep in touch with the care team. 3 Tesla magnetic resonance imaging for detailed views of soft tissues, the brain, spine and joints.

Imaging of blood vessels for diagnosis and to guide treatment.
Measurement of bone density to assess osteoporosis.

Outpatient examination by a medical geneticist to assess whether a genetic condition may be present.

Medical genetics diagnoses inherited and non-inherited conditions caused by changes in genes, and helps individuals and families understand their risks, including carrier status and risks for future children. The genetic diagnosis centre at our partner hospital offers genetic consultations and counselling alongside cytogenetic, molecular cytogenetic and molecular genetic testing in ISO 15189 accredited laboratories. MedLuxLife coordinates your appointments and the practical steps of your visit.
Rapid assessment of suspicious tissue during surgery, available at any time of day, to support decisions in the operating theatre.
Biopsy samples are reported within a few working days, depending on their nature.
Accelerated processing when cancer is suspected or urgent treatment is needed, so a preliminary diagnosis can be reached without delay.
Staining panels, manual or automated, that help determine tumour origin, classification, proliferation index and prognostic markers.
Diagnostic histochemical and immunohistochemical staining and immunofluorescence studies, with daily automated processing.
PCR, flow cytometry and in situ hybridisation carried out jointly with the microbiology and genetics laboratories.
Liquid-based and conventional cytology, with immunocytochemistry when needed.
Pathologists check sample adequacy on site while interventional teams take diagnostic samples.
Paraffin blocks and slides for review, if a second opinion is requested

Medical pathology examines tissue and cell samples to establish a diagnosis and guide treatment, with an emphasis on fast and accurate reporting. The department at our partner hospital includes immunohistochemistry and cytopathology laboratories and works with the microbiology and genetics laboratories for advanced methods. MedLuxLife coordinates the practical steps of your visit; existing samples and reports are arranged directly with the partner hospital.

Medical microbiology provides the laboratory testing behind the diagnosis and treatment of infections. The laboratories at our partner hospital support inpatient, outpatient and emergency care across bacteriology, virology, parasitology, mycology, molecular microbiology and infection immunology, with a broad and regularly updated test panel. MedLuxLife coordinates sample collection during your visit and ensures your results are translated and shared with your doctors.
Identification of bacteria and antibiotic susceptibility testing, combining classical culture with rapid confirmatory methods and same-day stained microscopy.
Isolation and identification of acid-fast organisms such as Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Mycobacterium avium complex, including molecular methods and the Quantiferon TB Gold test.
Antigen and antibody serology, sensitive detection of HIV and hepatitis agents, and confirmatory testing where needed.
Diagnosis of parasitic infections using classical methods supported by serological tests.
Identification of yeasts, dermatophytes and moulds, plus galactomannan antigen testing for suspected aspergillus infection in immunocompromised patients.
PCR-based detection, genotyping and viral load testing, including viruses monitored after transplantation.
Rapid multiplex testing of blood cultures, respiratory, gastrointestinal, cerebrospinal and joint fluid samples, with simultaneous detection of resistance genes.
Immunological tests that support the diagnosis of infectious diseases.
The laboratory operates 24 hours a day and works closely with clinicians on diagnosis and treatment.
Bacterial culture and antibiotic susceptibility testing
Syndromic panels for blood culture, respiratory, gastrointestinal, CSF and joint fluid samples
Previous culture, serology or PCR results

MedLuxLife can help you understand how this field relates to your care and connect you with the appropriate clinical specialists.
Examination of the microscopic features, structure and organisation of cells and tissues.
Study of how cells and tissues are built and how they work together.
Study of how organs form and develop from cells and tissues.
Study of development from fertilisation to birth.
Research into the causes of abnormal development during pregnancy.
